title: The Longitude Problem Solver
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Calculate longitude from the gap between local noon and a chronometer, then introduce a clock error and watch the ship slide across the ocean.

learningObjectives: Calculate longitude from a difference between local time and reference time.
Evaluate how a given clock error translates into a position error in kilometres.
prerequisites: Knowing that the Earth turns once in 24 hours

keyQuestions: Why is a clock the instrument that solves a position problem?
Your chronometer runs one minute fast. Do you think you are east or west of where you are?
Why was longitude harder to solve than latitude?
commonMisconceptions: Believing longitude can be measured directly from the sky the way latitude can.
Assuming a degree of longitude is the same distance everywhere.
Treating the clock as a convenience rather than as the measuring instrument.
assessmentOpportunities: Converts a time difference into a longitude without being given the 15 degrees per hour rule.
Predicts the direction the calculated position moves when the chronometer runs fast.
Explains why the same clock error matters less at high latitude.
